newsitem.title: UK: IPE natural gas seen directionless, quiet.
newsitem.headline: IPE natural gas seen directionless, quiet.

text.p: IPE natural gas brokers were uncertain as to the market's price direction on Monday with transport disruptions in London likely to stifle early trade even more than usual.
"I do not know where it is going - nobody seems to be at their desks," one said.
Five main railway stations in the capital were closed on Monday morning after police received coded bomb warnings, bringing central London almost to a standstill.
A dealer in the physical gas market said he was not aware of any fundamental factors over the weekend which were likely to have an impact on prices.
"All I know is that it has been very cold in the mornings - that could have a little effect."
The Met Office said in its 24-hour forecast, without further elaboration on the outlook for temperatures: "Frosty tonight."
Business on Friday afternoon was limited to a pitiful single five-lot trade, with front-month May trading down 0.125 pence pre therm at 10.25 pence.
Physical markets were busier on Friday, with most trade going on in the third quarter of the year.
